content.user_title: Build Programmatic SEO Pages at Scale
content.value_statement: Scaling SEO pages can create thin content, weak links, and poor indexation. This skill guides data-driven page templates, playbooks, and quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Selects suitable programmatic SEO playbooks for a business model.
Defines page variables, data requirements, and template sections.
Recommends clean URL structures for scaled page sets.
Plans internal linking with hub, spoke, and related page patterns.
Creates launch and monitoring checklists for indexation quality.
Identifies common risks such as thin content and keyword cannibalization.
limitations: Does not perform live keyword research without user-provided data or tools.
Does not generate final production pages by itself.
Does not guarantee ranking, traffic, or indexation outcomes.
Requires accurate business, audience, and data source context.

use_cases.title: Plan a Local Page System
use_cases.description: Design location pages with unique local value, clean URLs, and crawlable internal links.

use_cases.title: Build a Directory SEO Strategy
use_cases.description: Turn structured company, product, or profile data into useful directory pages.

use_cases.title: Improve Scaled Page Indexation
use_cases.description: Diagnose thin content, crawl budget, sitemap, and linking issues across existing page sets.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Playbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a programmatic SEO playbook for my business. Ask for any missing context before recommending a page pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Design Page Templates
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a page template for [keyword pattern]. Include URL structure, title ideas, unique sections, data fields, and internal links.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Page Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this programmatic SEO plan for thin content, duplicate pages, weak data, indexation risks, and missing quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Indexation Recovery Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: We launched [number] programmatic pages and only [number] are indexed. Diagnose likely causes and create a prioritized recovery plan.

output_examples.input: I want to create pages for accounting software integrations.
output: Primary URL pattern: integrations by product name.
Required data: supported actions, setup steps, screenshots, use cases, and limitations.
Quality focus: prove each integration works and avoid placeholder pages.

output_examples.input: We have 500 location pages and most are not indexed.
output: Likely issues include thin local content, weak internal links, and sitemap quality.
Prioritize pages with real demand and stronger local proof.
Noindex weak variations until each page has unique user value.

output_examples.input: Create a quality checklist for template pages.
output: Each page should offer a usable asset, not only a preview.
Titles and descriptions should be unique.
Related templates should link to each other and to a hub page.

best_practices: Start with search intent, available data, and page-level user value.
Use subfolders, hub pages, breadcrumbs, and related links to support discovery.
Launch fewer strong pages before expanding to larger page sets.
anti_patterns: Creating thousands of pages by changing only a city, keyword, or product name.
Publishing pages with no search demand, no data source, or no conversion goal.
Using scraped or stale public data without adding original analysis.

faq.question: What is programmatic SEO?
faq.answer: Programmatic SEO uses templates and structured data to create many useful pages for repeated search patterns.

faq.question: Can this skill help avoid thin content?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes unique page value, data quality, intent match, and quality checks before launch.

faq.question: Does it do keyword research automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can guide research, but it needs user-provided keyword data or access to separate SEO tools.

faq.question: Which page types does it support?
faq.answer: It covers templates, directories, comparisons, locations, integrations, glossaries, profiles, translations, and related playbooks.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot indexing problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews content uniqueness, internal links, crawl paths, sitemap inclusion, and noindex conflicts.

faq.question: Is it only for large websites?
faq.answer: No. Small teams can use it to test focused page sets before scaling.
